groups.title: Quest definitions: JSON files listing acceptance criteria that checker.py evaluates

checks.why: the summary quest through the real checker

risks.text: A criterion type other than contains, max_chars or min_chars (e.g. a typo) silently always fails instead of erroring.

Every criterion needs a type and description, and a quest needs acceptance_criteria; a missing key crashes the checker with a KeyError, and a missing value on a numeric criterion crashes with a TypeError.
Character limits count the raw submission text including any trailing newline, so a limit like 280 or 60 is hit by a file ending in a newline.
tagline.json has no test; changing its limits is unverified.

groups.title: The checker script that grades a submission file against a quest, plus README and license

checks.why: pass and fail paths of the checker
the CLI end to end (README usage; exit code 1 on any failure)

risks.text: The CLI opens the quest and submission files without an explicit encoding, so results depend on the platform locale and non-ASCII text can crash or change character counts.
The submission is read raw: trailing newline and whitespace are kept and counted by min_chars/max_chars and compared by contains.
Arguments are read from sys.argv with no validation and the files are never closed; missing arguments or files give a raw traceback, not a clean refusal.
A quest with an empty acceptance_criteria list makes all([]) true, so any submission passes and the CLI exits 0.
Unknown criterion types fail (ok=False) rather than raise, and the exit code is the only machine signal of failure.

groups.title: Pytest tests for the checker against the summary quest

risks.text: Tests locate quests/summary.json and checker.py by paths relative to the test file (and edit sys.path); renaming or moving either file breaks them.
Only the summary quest is covered; min_chars, tagline and unknown criterion types have no tests.

rules.rule: Every quest file lists at least one acceptance criterion (README states this); the checker does not enforce it.
rules.why: With an empty list all([]) is true, so every submission passes and the quest checks nothing.

checks.why: runs a quest through the CLI; with zero criteria it would print nothing and exit 0, so output must show criteria lines

rules.rule: checker.py exits 0 only when every criterion passed, and 1 otherwise.
rules.why: Callers and scripts use the exit code to accept or reject a submission.

checks.why: runs the CLI on a real quest; expected to exit 1 (FAIL lines), showing the exit code follows the criteria

rules.rule: An unrecognised criterion type counts as failed, never as passed.
rules.why: Passing it would let a submission through unchecked.
